claim: Disrupting the glycolytic gene phosphoglycerate kinase-1 (pgk1) impairs Fgf-dependent development of hair cells and neurons in the otic vesicle.
source: Using forward and reverse genetics in zebrafish, we show that disrupting the glycolytic gene phosphoglycerate kinase-1 (pgk1) impairs Fgf-dependent development of hair cells and neurons in the otic vesicle and other neurons in the CNS/PNS.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on genetic experiments in zebrafish.

claim: Disrupting pgk1 impairs Fgf-dependent development of other neurons in the CNS/PNS.
source: Using forward and reverse genetics in zebrafish, we show that disrupting the glycolytic gene phosphoglycerate kinase-1 (pgk1) impairs Fgf-dependent development of hair cells and neurons in the otic vesicle and other neurons in the CNS/PNS.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on genetic experiments.

claim: Fgf-MAPK signaling underperforms in pgk1-/- mutants even when Fgf is transiently overexpressed.
source: Fgf-MAPK signaling underperforms in pgk1- / - mutants even when Fgf is transiently overexpressed.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this observation from experimental data.

claim: Wild-type embryos treated with drugs that block synthesis or secretion of lactate mimic the pgk1-/- phenotype.
source: Wild-type embryos treated with drugs that block synthesis or secretion of lactate mimic the pgk1- / - phenotype, whereas pgk1- / - mutants are rescued by treatment with exogenous lactate.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from pharmacological experiments.

claim: pgk1-/- mutants are rescued by treatment with exogenous lactate.
source: Wild-type embryos treated with drugs that block synthesis or secretion of lactate mimic the pgk1- / - phenotype, whereas pgk1- / - mutants are rescued by treatment with exogenous lactate.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this rescue experiment result.

claim: Lactate treatment of wild-type embryos elevates expression of Etv5b/Erm even when Fgf signaling is blocked.
source: Lactate treatment of wild-type embryos elevates expression of Etv5b/Erm even when Fgf signaling is blocked.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from experimental manipulation.

claim: Lactate's ability to stimulate neurogenesis is reversed by blocking MAPK.
source: However, lactate's ability to stimulate neurogenesis is reversed by blocking MAPK.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from inhibitor experiments.

claim: Lactate raises basal levels of MAPK and Etv5b, rendering cells more responsive to dynamic changes in Fgf signaling.
source: Thus, lactate raises basal levels of MAPK and Etv5b (a critical effector of the Fgf pathway), rendering cells more responsive to dynamic changes in Fgf signaling required by many developing tissues.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this mechanistic conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The otic placode produces the entire inner ear.
source: Of the cranial placodes, the developmental complexity of the otic placode is especially remarkable for producing the entire inner ear, with its convoluted epithelial labyrinth and rich cell type diversity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Hair cell specification is initiated by expression of Atoh1.
source: Hair cell specification is initiated by expression of the bHLH factor Atonal Homolog 1 (Atoh1) (Bermingham et al., 1999; Chen et al., 2002; Millimaki et al., 2007; Raft et al., 2007; Woods et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Atoh1 activates expression of Notch ligands that mediate specification of support cells via lateral inhibition.
source: Atoh1 subsequently activates expression of Notch ligands that mediate specification of support cells via lateral inhibition.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Specification of SAG neuroblasts is initiated by localized expression of Neurogenin1 (Ngn1).
source: Specification of SAG neuroblasts is initiated by localized expression of the bHLH factor Neurogenin1 (Ngn1) (Andermann et al., 2002; Korzh et al., 1998; Ma et al., 1998; Raft et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Fgf-dependent induction of Ngn1 establishes the neurogenic domain during placodal stages in chick and mouse embryos.
source: Fgf-dependent induction of Ngn1 establishes the neurogenic domain during placodal stages, marking one of the earliest molecular asymmetries in the otic placode in chick and mouse embryos (Abelló et al., 2010; Alsina et al., 2004; Magariños et al., 2010; Mansour et al., 1993; Pirvola et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Fgf specifies sensory domains of Atoh1 expression as neurogenesis subsides.
source: Subsequently, as neurogenesis subsides, Fgf also specifies sensory domains of Atoh1 expression (Hayashi et al., 2008; Ono et al., 2014; Pirvola et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In zebrafish, sensory domains form precociously during the earliest stages of otic induction in response to Fgf from the hindbrain and subjacent mesoderm.
source: In zebrafish, sensory domains form precociously during the earliest stages of otic induction in response to Fgf from the hindbrain and subjacent mesoderm (Gou et al., 2018; Millimaki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Rising levels of Fgf eventually exceed an upper threshold to terminate further specification of neuroblasts.
source: As more neurons accumulate, rising levels of Fgf eventually exceed an upper threshold to terminate further specification of neuroblasts and delay differentiation of transit-amplifying SAG progenitors (Vemaraju et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Elevated Fgf inhibits further hair cell specification while maintaining support cells in a quiescent state.
source: Additionally, elevated Fgf inhibits further hair cell specification while maintaining support cells in a quiescent state (Bermingham-McDonogh et al., 2001; Jiang et al., 2014; Ku et al., 2014; Maier and Whitfield, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Populations of proliferating stem cells or progenitors modify glycolysis by shunting pyruvate away from mitochondrial respiration in favor of lactate synthesis, despite an abundance of free oxygen.
source: For example, populations of proliferating stem cells or progenitors, including human embryonic stem cells, neural stem cells, hematopoietic stem cells, and posterior presomitic mesoderm, modify glycolysis by shunting pyruvate away from mitochondrial respiration in favor of lactate synthesis, despite an abundance of free oxygen (Agathocleous et al., 2012; Bulusu et al., 2017; Gu et al., 2016; Oginuma et al., 2017; Sá et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2014; Zheng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis is thought to be an adaptation for accelerating ATP synthesis while simultaneously producing carbon chains needed for rapid biosynthesis.
source: This is similar to 'aerobic glycolysis' (also known as the 'Warburg Effect') exhibited by metastatic tumors, thought to be an adaptation for accelerating ATP synthesis while simultaneously producing carbon chains needed for rapid biosynthesis (Liberti and Locasale, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Aerobic glycolysis promotes cell signaling to stimulate differentiation of osteoblasts, myocardial cells, and fast twitch muscle.
source: For example, aerobic glycolysis promotes relevant cell signaling to stimulate differentiation of osteoblasts, myocardial cells, and fast twitch muscle (Esen et al., 2013; Menendez-Montes et al., 2016; Ozbudak et al., 2010; Tixier et al., 2013), as well as maintenance of cone cells in the retina (Aït-Ali et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Two independent mutations that disrupt Phosphoglycerate Kinase 1 (Pgk1) were recovered in a screen to identify novel regulators of SAG development in zebrafish.
source: In a screen to identify novel regulators of SAG development in zebrafish, we recovered two independent mutations that disrupt the glycolytic enzyme Phosphoglycerate Kinase 1 (Pgk1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from the screen.

claim: Loss of Pgk1 causes a delay in upregulation of Fgf signaling in the otic vesicle.
source: Loss of Pgk1 causes a delay in upregulation of Fgf signaling in the otic vesicle, causing a deficiency in early neural and sensory development.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Pgk1 is co-expressed with Fgf ligands in the otic vesicle, olfactory epithelium and various clusters of neurons in cranial ganglia and the neural tube.
source: We show that Pgk1 is co-expressed with Fgf ligands in the otic vesicle, as well as in the olfactory epithelium and various clusters of neurons in cranial ganglia and the neural tube.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from expression analysis.

claim: Pgk1 acts non-autonomously to promote Fgf signaling at a distance by promoting synthesis and secretion of lactate.
source: Moreover, Pgk1 acts non-autonomously to promote Fgf signaling at a distance by promoting synthesis and secretion of lactate.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Lactate independently activates the MAPK pathway, leading to elevated expression of the effector Etv5b.
source: Lactate independently activates the MAPK pathway, leading to elevated expression of the effector Etv5b, priming the pathway to render cells more responsive to dynamic changes in Fgf levels.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from the study.

claim: sagd1-/- mutants show a ~60% deficiency in anterior SAG neurons at 24 and 30 hpf.
source: Quantification of isl2b:Gfp+ cells in serial sections of sagd1- / - mutants revealed a ~ 60% deficiency in anterior SAG neurons (which are essential for vestibular function) at 24 and 30 hpf (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by quantification shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The number of anterior neurons in sagd1-/- mutants remained lower than normal through at least 48 hpf.
source: The number of anterior neurons remained lower than normal through at least 48 hpf whereas accumulation of posterior SAG neurons (which includes auditory neurons) appeared normal (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: Accumulation of posterior SAG neurons appeared normal in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: The number of anterior neurons remained lower than normal through at least 48 hpf whereas accumulation of posterior SAG neurons (which includes auditory neurons) appeared normal (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: The early deficit of SAG neurons in sagd1-/- mutants did not result from increased apoptosis.
source: Of note, the early deficit of SAG neurons did not result from increased apoptosis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J), and in fact sagd1- / - mutants produced fewer apoptotic cells than normal.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by TUNEL assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1J.

claim: sagd1-/- mutants show deficits in balance and motor coordination indicative of vestibular dysfunction.
source: sagd1- / - mutants show no overt defects in gross morphology, although sagd1- / - mutants do show deficits in balance and motor coordination indicative of vestibular dysfunction.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observed phenotype.

claim: sagd1-/- mutants typically die by 10-12 dpf.
source: Mutants typically die by 10–12 dpf.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observed phenotype.

claim: Early stages of neuroblast specification were significantly impaired in sagd1-/- mutants, with only 30% of the normal number of ngn1+ neuroblasts inside the otic vesicle at 24 hpf.
source: We observed that early stages of neuroblast specification were significantly impaired in sagd1- / - mutants, with only 30% of the normal number of ngn1+ neuroblasts inside the otic vesicle at 24 hpf (Figure 1C,D,G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1G.

claim: The number of ngn1+ neuroblasts in the otic vesicle was normal by 30 hpf in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: However, subsequent stages of neural specification gradually improved in sagd1- / - mutants, such that the number of ngn1+ neuroblasts in the otic vesicle was normal by 30 hpf (Figure 1E,F,G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1G.

claim: In sagd1-/- mutants, the number of ngn1+ neuroblasts outside the otic vesicle was reduced by 50-60% at every stage examined.
source: In sagd1- / - mutants, the number of ngn1+ neuroblasts outside the otic vesicle was reduced by 50–60% at every stage examined (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1H.

claim: The number of neurod+ transit-amplifying cells was strongly reduced in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Similarly, the number of neurod+ transit-amplifying cells was strongly reduced in sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 1I–Q).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1Q.

claim: The deficit in neurod+ cells was more pronounced at 30 hpf (~60% decrease) than at 48 hpf (~20% decrease) in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: This deficit was more pronounced at 30 hpf (~60% decrease) than at 48 hpf (~20% decrease).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 1Q.

claim: Expression of atoh1a was reduced in both anterior (utricular) and posterior (saccular) maculae at 24 and 30 hpf in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Expression of prosensory marker atoh1a was reduced in both anterior (utricular) and posterior (saccular) maculae at 24 and 30 hpf (Figure 2A–B').
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by images in Figure 2A-B'.

claim: sagd1-/- mutants produced roughly 25% fewer than normal hair cells in the utricle and saccule at 36 and 48 hpf.
source: In agreement, sagd1- / - mutants produced roughly 25% fewer than normal hair cells in the utricle and saccule at 36 and 48 hpf (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by quantification in Figure 2E.

claim: Expression of fgf3 and fgf8a appeared relatively normal in sagd1-/- mutants from 18 to 30 hpf.
source: Expression of fgf3 and fgf8a appeared relatively normal in sagd1- / - mutants from 18 to 30 hpf (Figure 2S–T', and data not shown).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by images in Figure 2S-T'.

claim: Expression of downstream Fgf-targets etv5b, pax5 and sprouty4 were severely deficient in the otic vesicle of sagd1-/- mutants at 18 hpf.
source: However, expression of downstream Fgf-targets etv5b, pax5 and sprouty4 were severely deficient in the otic vesicle of sagd1- / - mutants at 18 hpf (Figure 2F–H').
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by images in Figure 2F-H'.

claim: Expression of etv5b, pax5 and sprouty4 partially recovered by 21 hpf and was only mildly reduced by 24 hpf in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Expression of these genes partially recovered by 21 hpf and was only mildly reduced by 24 hpf (Figure 2I–N').
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by images in Figure 2I-N'.

claim: Markers of axial identity were largely unaffected at 30 hpf in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Despite these changes, markers of axial identity were largely unaffected at 30 hpf, including the dorsal marker dlx3b, the ventrolateral marker otx1, the anteromedial marker pax5 and posteromedial marker pou3f3b (Figure 2O–R').
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by images in Figure 2O-R'.

claim: The zebrafish genome harbors only one pgk1 gene.
source: The zebrafish genome harbors only one pgk1 gene, but the locus produces two distinct transcripts (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from genomic analysis.

claim: The pgk1 locus produces two distinct transcripts.
source: The zebrafish genome harbors only one pgk1 gene, but the locus produces two distinct transcripts (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: The primary transcript (pgk1-FL) encodes full-length Pgk1, which is highly conserved amongst vertebrates (nearly 90% identical between zebrafish and human).
source: The primary transcript (pgk1-FL) encodes full-length Pgk1, which is highly conserved amongst vertebrates (nearly 90% identical between zebrafish and human).
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from sequence analysis.

claim: The pgk1-alt transcript arises from an independent transcription start site in the first intron of pgk1-FL.
source: However, the second pgk1 transcript, termed pgk1-alt, is unique to zebrafish and arises from an independent transcription start site in the first intron of pgk1-FL.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from transcript analysis.

claim: The pgk1-alt transcript is unique to zebrafish.
source: However, the second pgk1 transcript, termed pgk1-alt, is unique to zebrafish and arises from an independent transcription start site in the first intron of pgk1-FL.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from comparative analysis.

claim: pgk1-alt encodes a truncated protein that includes much of the N-terminal half of Pgk1 but presumably lacks glycolytic enzyme activity.
source: Thus pgk1-alt encodes a truncated protein that includes much of the N-terminal half of Pgk1 but presumably lacks glycolytic enzyme activity as the C-terminal peptide is required for ADP/ATP binding.
evidence: This is explicitly stated based on sequence analysis and known protein structure.

claim: In sagd1-/- mutants, pgk1-alt contains two nucleotide substitutions leading to loss of a splice acceptor site as well as the translation start codon in exon 1b.
source: In sagd1- / - mutants, pgk1-alt contains two nucleotide substitutions leading to loss of a splice acceptor site as well as the translation start codon in exon 1b (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: pgk1-alt transcript abundance is strongly reduced in sagd1 mutants.
source: pgk1-alt transcript abundance is strongly reduced in sagd1 mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Injecting wild-type embryos with a splice-blocker to target the exon 1b splice acceptor site impaired accumulation of pgk1-alt transcript.
source: Injecting wild-type embryos with a splice-blocker to target the exon 1b splice acceptor site (sbMO, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) impaired accumulation of pgk1-alt transcript (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B) and reduced accumulation of Isl1+ SAG neurons by nearly 40% (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B-C.

claim: Injecting wild-type embryos with a splice-blocker to target the exon 1b splice acceptor site reduced accumulation of Isl1+ SAG neurons by nearly 40%.
source: Injecting wild-type embryos with a splice-blocker to target the exon 1b splice acceptor site (sbMO, Figure 3—figure supplement 3A) impaired accumulation of pgk1-alt transcript (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B) and reduced accumulation of Isl1+ SAG neurons by nearly 40% (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Injecting either translation blocker alone, or in combination, reduced accumulation of Isl1+ SAG neurons by 20-30%.
source: Injecting either translation blocker alone, or in combination, reduced accumulation of Isl1+ SAG neurons by 20–30% (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Translation blockers impaired accumulation of pgk1-alt transcript.
source: Interestingly, the translation blockers also impaired accumulation of pgk1-alt transcript (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B), suggesting that Pgk1-alt protein is required for normal transcript accumulation.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Pgk1-alt protein is required for normal transcript accumulation.
source: Interestingly, the translation blockers also impaired accumulation of pgk1-alt transcript (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B), suggesting that Pgk1-alt protein is required for normal transcript accumulation.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the morpholino data.

claim: pgk1-FL transcript is maternally deposited and is widely expressed at a low level during subsequent stages of development in wild-type embryos.
source: In wild-type embryos pgk1-FL transcript (but not pgk1-alt) is maternally deposited and is widely expressed at a low level during subsequent stages of development (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4A.

claim: By 14 hpf pgk1-FL upregulates in developing somites.
source: By 14 hpf pgk1-FL upregulates in developing somites (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B), and beginning around 18–20 hpf pgk1-FL transcript abundance becomes elevated in clusters of cells scattered throughout the central and peripheral nervous systems (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C–E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Beginning around 18-20 hpf pgk1-FL transcript abundance becomes elevated in clusters of cells scattered throughout the central and peripheral nervous systems.
source: By 14 hpf pgk1-FL upregulates in developing somites (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B), and beginning around 18–20 hpf pgk1-FL transcript abundance becomes elevated in clusters of cells scattered throughout the central and peripheral nervous systems (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C–E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4C-E.

claim: Local upregulation of pgk1-FL and pgk1-alt is severely attenuated in the nervous system in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Local upregulation of pgk1-FL and pgk1-alt is severely attenuated in the nervous system in sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 3D–R), whereas expression remains elevated in somites (data not shown).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3D-R.

claim: When hs:pgk1-alt was activated at 20 hpf, accumulation of pgk1-FL was markedly elevated at 23-24 hpf.
source: When hs:pgk1-alt was activated at 20 hpf, accumulation of pgk1-FL was markedly elevated at 23–24 hpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 5I–N).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5I-N.

claim: Transgenic pgk1-alt transcript peaked near the end of the heat shock period at 21 hpf but then decayed to background levels by 24 hpf.
source: This was in contrast to accumulation of transgenic pgk1-alt transcript, which peaked near the end of the heat shock period at 21 hpf but then decayed to background levels by 24 hpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A–H).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5A-H.

claim: Perdurance of Pgk1-alt protein is sufficient to upregulate pgk1-FL.
source: We infer that perdurance of Pgk1-alt protein is sufficient to upregulate pgk1-FL.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the heat shock experiment results.

claim: The pgk1x55 mutation is predicted to eliminate all but the first 19 amino acids of Pgk1.
source: This presumptive null mutation is predicted to eliminate all but the first 19 amino acids of Pgk1.
evidence: This is explicitly stated based on the sequence of the mutation.

claim: Expression of pgk1 is severely reduced in pgk1-/- mutants, presumably reflecting nonsense-mediated decay.
source: Expression of pgk1 is severely reduced in pgk1- / - mutants, presumably reflecting nonsense-mediated decay (Figure 3—figure supplement 4H).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4H.

claim: The phenotype of pgk1-/- mutants is nearly identical to sagd1-/-.
source: The phenotype of pgk1- / - mutants is nearly identical to sagd1-/-: Despite apparently normal early expression of fgf3 and fgf8a, pgk1- / - mutants show impaired responses to early Fgf signaling, including reduced otic expression of pax5 and etv5b at 18 hpf, reduced ngn1 at 24 hpf, a deficiency in neurod+ transit-amplifying cells at 24 hpf, and a deficiency in mature isl2b-gfp+ SAG neurons at 30 hpf (Figure 4A–H,Q; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4A-H,Q and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: pgk1-/- mutants showed a deficiency in both anterior and posterior SAG neurons (reduced 31% and 18%, respectively, at 5 dpf).
source: Unlike sagd1 mutants, however, pgk1- / - mutants showed a deficiency in both anterior and posterior SAG neurons (reduced 31% and 18%, respectively, at 5 dpf, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: pgk1-/- mutants showed a 20-25% decrease in the number of utricular and saccular hair cells at 36 hpf, 48 hpf and five dpf.
source: pgk1- / - mutants also showed a 20–25% decrease in the number of utricular and saccular hair cells at 36 hpf, 48 hpf and five dpf (Figure 4T).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4T.

claim: Other aspects of otic vesicle patterning appeared normal in pgk1-/- mutants based on expression of regional markers otx1, pou3f3b, hmx3a and dlx3b at 24 hpf.
source: Other aspects of otic vesicle patterning appeared normal based on expression of regional markers otx1, pou3f3b, hmx3a and dlx3b at 24 hpf (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Development of trigeminal, facial and glossopharyngeal ganglia, reticulospinal neurons in the hindbrain, and the olfactory epithelium are deficient in pgk1-/- mutants.
source: Beyond the inner ear, development of a number of other Fgf-dependent neural cell types are also deficient in pgk1- / - mutants, including trigeminal, facial and glossopharyngeal ganglia, reticulospinal neurons in the hindbrain, and the olfactory epithelium (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: pgk1-/- mutants eventually die around 10-12 days post-fertilization.
source: Although pgk1- / - mutants show overtly normal gross morphology, they eventually die around 10–12 days post-fertilization.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observed phenotype.

claim: When pgk1+/- heterozygotes were crossed with sagd1+/- heterozygotes, all intercross embryos developed normally.
source: When pgk1+ / - heterozygotes were crossed with sagd1+ / - heterozygotes, all intercross embryos developed normally (Figure 4Q), confirming that pgk1-alt and pgk1-FL encode distinct complementary functions.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4Q.

claim: pgk1-alt and pgk1-FL encode distinct complementary functions.
source: When pgk1+ / - heterozygotes were crossed with sagd1+ / - heterozygotes, all intercross embryos developed normally (Figure 4Q), confirming that pgk1-alt and pgk1-FL encode distinct complementary functions.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the genetic cross data.

claim: Activation of hs:pgk1 at 18 hpf rescued the SAG deficiency in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Activation of hs:pgk1 at 18 hpf rescued the SAG deficiency in sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 4Q).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4Q.

claim: Activation of hs:pgk1-alt at 18 hpf was not able to rescue pgk1-/- mutants.
source: In contrast, activation of hs:pgk1-alt at 18 hpf was not able to rescue pgk1- / - mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A), whereas activation of hs:pgk1-alt at 18 hpf did rescue morphants injected with pgk1-alt-sbMO (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Activation of hs:pgk1-alt at 18 hpf rescued morphants injected with pgk1-alt-sbMO.
source: In contrast, activation of hs:pgk1-alt at 18 hpf was not able to rescue pgk1- / - mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A), whereas activation of hs:pgk1-alt at 18 hpf did rescue morphants injected with pgk1-alt-sbMO (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: pgk1-alt is required upstream to locally upregulate pgk1-FL.
source: Together, these data show that pgk1-alt is required upstream to locally upregulate pgk1-FL, which in turn is required for proper Fgf signaling and development of sensory hair cells, SAG neurons and various other Fgf-dependent neurons in the head.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the genetic and rescue experiments.

claim: pgk1-FL is required for proper Fgf signaling and development of sensory hair cells, SAG neurons and various other Fgf-dependent neurons in the head.
source: Together, these data show that pgk1-alt is required upstream to locally upregulate pgk1-FL, which in turn is required for proper Fgf signaling and development of sensory hair cells, SAG neurons and various other Fgf-dependent neurons in the head.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the genetic experiments.

claim: Sites of upregulation of pgk1-FL and pgk1-alt occur within or near sites of expression of various Fgf ligands.
source: We note that sites of upregulation of pgk1-FL and pgk1-alt occurs within or near sites of expression of various Fgf ligands, including sensory epithelia, mature SAG neurons, and other tissues depicted in Figure 3—figure supplement 4F–G (Reifers et al., 1998; Thisse et al., 2001; Millimaki et al., 2007; Feng and Xu, 2010; Terriente et al., 2012; Vemaraju et al., 2012).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by comparison with cited literature and Figure 3—figure supplement 4F-G.

claim: Local upregulation of pgk1 occurred normally in embryos treated with the Fgf pathway-inhibitor SU5402.
source: We found that local upregulation of pgk1 occurred normally in embryos treated with the Fgf pathway-inhibitor SU5402 (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: pgk1 and fgf genes are not required for each other's expression but could share a common upstream regulator.
source: Thus, pgk1 and fgf genes are not required for each other's expression but could share a common upstream regulator.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the inhibitor experiments.

claim: The majority of wild-type cells located near the utricular Fgf source in the floor of the otic vesicle in pgk1-/- hosts did not express the Fgf-target etv5b.
source: Surprisingly, the majority of the wild-type cells located near the utricular Fgf source in the floor of the otic vesicle in pkg1- / - hosts did not express the Fgf-target etv5b (Figure 4J,L,N,P,R).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4J,L,N,P,R.

claim: Wild-type cells transplanted into wild-type hosts showed normal expression of etv5b.
source: In control experiments, wild-type cells transplanted into wild-type hosts showed normal expression of etv5b (Figure 4I,K,M,O,R).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4I,K,M,O,R.

claim: Pgk1 is required non-autonomously to promote Fgf signaling at a distance.
source: Thus, Pgk1 is required non-autonomously to promote Fgf signaling at a distance.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the cell transplantation experiments.

claim: Tumor cells secrete Pgk1 to promote early stages of metastasis through modulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) and cell signaling.
source: First, tumor cells secrete Pgk1 to promote early stages of metastasis through modulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) and cell signaling (Chirico, 2011; Jung et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Secreted Pgk1 serves as a disulfide reductase leading to proteolytic cleavage of Plasmin.
source: The only specific molecular function identified for secreted Pgk1 is to serve as a disulfide reductase leading to proteolytic cleavage of Plasmin (Lay et al., 2000), a serine protease that cleaves Fgf as well as ECM proteins required for Fgf signaling (Botta et al., 2012; George et al., 2001; Meddahi et al., 1995; Schmidt et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Injection of plg-tbMO did not rescue or ameliorate the neural deficiency in sagd1-/- or pgk1-/- mutants.
source: Injection of plg-tbMO did not rescue or ameliorate the neural deficiency in sagd1- / - or pgk1- / - mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 6A.

claim: Injection of plg-sbMO effectively attenuated plg transcript but did not rescue pgk1-/- mutants.
source: Injection of plg-sbMO effectively attenuated plg transcript (Figure 4—figure supplement 6C) but did not rescue pgk1- / - mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 6B-C.

claim: The effects of pgk1-/- and sagd1-/- do not depend on accumulation of Plasmin.
source: Therefore the effects of pgk1- / - and sagd1- / - do not depend on accumulation of Plasmin.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the plasminogen knockdown experiments.

claim: Treating wild-type embryos with 2-deoxy-glucose (2DG) or 3PO to block early steps in glycolysis reduced the number of mature SAG neurons to a level similar to that of pgk1-/- or sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Treating wild-type embryos with 2-deoxy-glucose (2DG) (Nirenberg and Hogg, 1958) or 3PO (Clem et al., 2008) to block early steps in glycolysis (Figure 5A) reduced the number of mature SAG neurons to a level similar to that of pgk1- / - or sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: Treating wild-type embryos with DCA at 14 hpf mimicked the deficiency of SAG neurons seen in pgk1-/- and sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Treating wild-type embryos with DCA at 14 hpf mimicked the deficiency of SAG neurons seen in pgk1- / - and sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: Wild-type embryos treated with Galloflavin at 14 hpf displayed a deficiency of SAG neurons similar to pgk1-/- and sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Wild-type embryos treated with Galloflavin at 14 hpf also displayed a deficiency of SAG neurons similar to pgk1- / - and sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Application of CHC or UK5099 at 14 hpf mimicked the SAG deficiency in pgk1-/- and sagd1-/- mutants.
source: Application of either CHC or UK5099 at 14 hpf also mimicked the SAG deficiency in pgk1- / - and sagd1- / - mutants (Figure 5C, and data not shown).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Treatment of wild-type embryos with 2DG, Galloflavin or CHC reduced hair cell production to a level comparable to sagd1-/- or pgk1-/- mutants.
source: Treatment of wild-type embryos with 2DG, Galloflavin or CHC also reduced hair cell production to a level comparable to sagd1- / - or pgk1- / - mutants (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5D.

claim: Lactate treatment elevated SAG accumulation above normal in wild-type embryos and fully rescued pgk1-/- mutants.
source: As shown in Figure 5C, lactate treatment elevated SAG accumulation above normal in wild-type embryos and fully rescued pgk1- / - mutants.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: Lactate treatment rescued hair cell production in wild-type embryos treated with 2DG, Galloflavin, or CHC.
source: Lactate treatment also rescued hair cell production in wild-type embryos treated with 2DG, Galloflavin, or CHC (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5D.

claim: Pharmacological agents that block glycolysis, lactate synthesis or lactate secretion are sufficient to mimic the pgk1-/- and sagd1-/- phenotype.
source: Thus, pharmacological agents that block glycolysis, lactate synthesis or lactate secretion are sufficient to mimic the pgk1- / - and sagd1- / - phenotype, and exogenous lactate is sufficient to reverse these effects.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Exogenous lactate is sufficient to reverse the effects of blocking glycolysis, lactate synthesis or lactate secretion.
source: Thus, pharmacological agents that block glycolysis, lactate synthesis or lactate secretion are sufficient to mimic the pgk1- / - and sagd1- / - phenotype, and exogenous lactate is sufficient to reverse these effects.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Treatment of wild-type embryos with Galloflavin or CHC reduced the number of cells expressing etv5b and ngn1 at 18 hpf and 24 hpf, respectively.
source: Treatment of wild-type embryos with Galloflavin or CHC reduced the number of cells expressing etv5b and ngn1 at 18 hpf and 24 hpf, respectively (Figure 6Ag, Ah, Bg, Bh, E), mimicking the effects of pgk1-/- (Figure 6Ab, Bb, C, D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Treatment with exogenous lactate reversed the effects of Galloflavin and CHC on etv5b and ngn1 expression.
source: Treatment with exogenous lactate reversed the effects of Galloflavin and CHC (Figure 6Ai, Aj, Bj) and rescued pgk1- / - mutants (Figure 6Ac, Bc, C, D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Treating wild-type embryos with lactate increased the number of cells expressing etv5b and ngn1.
source: Moreover, treating wild-type embryos with lactate increased the number of cells expressing etv5b and ngn1 (Figure 6Ae, Be, C, D).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Adding exogenous ATP to pgk1-/- mutants at 14 hpf did not ameliorate the deficiency in expression of etv5b, ngn1, or pax5.
source: Adding exogenous ATP to pgk1- / - mutants at 14 hpf did not ameliorate the deficiency in expression of etv5b, ngn1, or pax5 (Figure 6Ad, Bd, C, D; and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adding ATP to wild-type embryos at 14 hpf did not significantly affect expression of etv5b, ngn1, or pax5.
source: Likewise, adding ATP to wild-type embryos at 14 hpf did not significantly affect expression of these genes (Figure 6Af, Bf, C, D; and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adding 25 uM sodium azide to wild-type embryos at 14 hpf to block mitochondrial respiration did not significantly impair expression of ngn1 at 24 hpf.
source: Finally, adding 25 uM sodium azide to wild-type embryos at 14 hpf to block mitochondrial respiration did not significantly impair expression of ngn1 at 24 hpf (Figure 6Bk, E).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Lactate is critical for early Fgf signaling and SAG specification.
source: Thus, lactate is critical for early Fgf signaling and SAG specification, but exogenous ATP does not affect these functions.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the ATP and azide experiments.

claim: Exogenous ATP does not affect early Fgf signaling and SAG specification.
source: Thus, lactate is critical for early Fgf signaling and SAG specification, but exogenous ATP does not affect these functions.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the ATP experiments.

claim: The deficiencies in otic development observed in pgk1-/- mutants can be attributed to disruption of lactate synthesis and secretion.
source: Moreover, the deficiencies in otic development observed in pgk1- / - mutants can be attributed to disruption of lactate synthesis and secretion.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the pharmacological and rescue experiments.

claim: Treatment of wild-type embryos with U0126 reduced the number of ngn1+ cells at 24 hpf and mature Isl1+ SAG neurons at 30 hpf to a degree similar to or greater than pgk1-/- mutants.
source: Treatment of wild-type embryos with U0126, an inhibitor of the MAPK activator Mek (Hawkins et al., 2008), reduced the number of ngn1+ cells at 24 hpf (Figure 6Bl, E) and mature Isl1+ SAG neurons at 30 hpf (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) to a degree similar to or greater than pgk1- / - mutants.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Treatment of wild-type embryos with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 had negligible effects on ngn1+ cells and SAG neurons.
source: In contrast, treatment of wild-type embryos with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (Montero et al., 2003) had negligible effects on these genes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, and data not shown), showing that most of the effects of Fgf are mediated by MAPK/Erk.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Most of the effects of Fgf on otic development are mediated by MAPK/Erk.
source: In contrast, treatment of wild-type embryos with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (Montero et al., 2003) had negligible effects on these genes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, and data not shown), showing that most of the effects of Fgf are mediated by MAPK/Erk.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the inhibitor experiments.

claim: Lactate can activate the MAPK/Erk pathway through Ras-independent activation of Raf kinase.
source: Recent findings show that lactate can activate the MAPK/Erk pathway through Ras-independent activation of Raf kinase (Lee et al., 2015), see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The ability of lactate to stimulate production of SAG neurons was completely blocked by co-treatment with U0126.
source: Consistent with this mechanism, the ability of lactate to stimulate production of SAG neurons was completely blocked by co-treatment with U0126 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Transient misexpression of dominant negative Fgf receptor fully suppressed etv5b expression within two hours of heat shock.
source: Transient misexpression of dominant negative Fgf receptor from a heat shock-inducible transgene, hs:dnfgfr1, fully suppressed etv5b expression within two hours of heat shock (Figure 6Ak; Figure 7C) and reduced accumulation of SAG neurons by 25% at 30 hpf (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6Ak, Figure 7C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Treatment with exogenous lactate partially restored etv5b expression when Fgf signaling was blocked.
source: Importantly, treatment with exogenous lactate partially restored etv5b expression when Fgf signaling was blocked (Figure 6Al; Figure 7D), although this was not sufficient to restore development of SAG neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6Al, Figure 7D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Lactate treatment was not sufficient to restore development of SAG neurons when Fgf signaling was blocked.
source: Importantly, treatment with exogenous lactate partially restored etv5b expression when Fgf signaling was blocked (Figure 6Al; Figure 7D), although this was not sufficient to restore development of SAG neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Activation of hs:fgf8 at a moderate level beginning at 16 hpf increased the level of pax5 expression in the otic vesicle at 18 hpf and expanded the spatial domain.
source: Activation of hs:fgf8 at a moderate level (37°C for 30 min) beginning at 16 hpf increased the level of pax5 expression in the otic vesicle at 18 hpf and expanded the spatial domain (Figure 7E,G).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 7E,G.

claim: Activation of hs:fgf8 in pgk1-/- mutants increased expression of pax5 relative to pgk1-/- alone, but not to the same degree seen in non-mutant embryos.
source: Activation of hs:fgf8 in pgk1- / - mutants increased expression of pax5 relative to pgk1- / - alone (Figure 7F,H), but not to the same degree seen in non-mutant embryos.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 7F,H.

claim: Elevating either Fgf or lactate alone can partially compensate for loss of the other.
source: Thus, elevating either Fgf or lactate alone can partially compensate for loss of the other, but full activation of early otic genes requires both Fgf and lactate to fully activate the MAPK/Erk pathway.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the rescue experiments.

claim: Full activation of early otic genes requires both Fgf and lactate to fully activate the MAPK/Erk pathway.
source: Thus, elevating either Fgf or lactate alone can partially compensate for loss of the other, but full activation of early otic genes requires both Fgf and lactate to fully activate the MAPK/Erk pathway.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the rescue experiments.

claim: Lactate binds and stabilizes the cytosolic protein Ndrg3, which in turn activates Raf.
source: Lactate has been shown to bind and stabilize the cytosolic protein Ndrg3, which in turn activates Raf (Lee et al., 2015) thereby converging with Fgf signaling to activate MAPK/Erk.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The MAPK/Erk pathway activates transcription of etv4 and etv5a/b genes.
source: The MAPK/Erk pathway activates transcription of etv4 and etv5a/b genes (Raible and Brand, 2001; Roehl and Nüsslein-Volhard, 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Etv4/5 proteins are phosphorylated and activated by MAPK/Erk and mediate many of the downstream effects of Fgf.
source: Etv4/5 proteins are also phosphorylated and activated by MAPK/Erk and mediate many of the downstream effects of Fgf (Brown et al., 1998; O'Hagan et al., 1996; Znosko et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Initial activation of MAPK/Erk by lactate would expand the pool of Etv4/5, priming cells to respond more quickly to dynamic changes in Fgf signaling.
source: Specifically, initial activation of MAPK/Erk by lactate would expand the pool of Etv4/5, priming cells to respond more quickly to dynamic changes in Fgf signaling.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a mechanistic explanation based on the experimental findings.

claim: Without pgk1, the initial response to Fgf is sluggish and causes lasting deficits in SAG neurons and slows accumulation of hair cells.
source: Without pgk1, the initial response to Fgf is sluggish and causes lasting deficits in SAG neurons and slows accumulation of hair cells.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the mutant phenotype analysis.

claim: As Fgf-mediated feedback amplification continues, Fgf signaling gradually improves on its own and is sufficient to support normal development of posterior SAG neurons in sagd1 mutants.
source: Later, as Fgf-mediated feedback amplification continues, Fgf signaling gradually improves on its own and is sufficient to support normal development of posterior SAG neurons in sagd1 mutants, although accumulation of SAG neurons and hair cell continues at a slower pace in pgk1- / - mutants.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an explanation for the temporal recovery observed in mutants.

claim: Accumulation of SAG neurons and hair cells continues at a slower pace in pgk1-/- mutants.
source: Later, as Fgf-mediated feedback amplification continues, Fgf signaling gradually improves on its own and is sufficient to support normal development of posterior SAG neurons in sagd1 mutants, although accumulation of SAG neurons and hair cell continues at a slower pace in pgk1- / - mutants.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observed phenotype.

claim: Upregulation of pgk1 in the otic vesicle is limited to sensory epithelia and mature SAG neurons.
source: Clearly wild type cells retain the ability to perform glycolysis, but since upregulation of pgk1 in the otic vesicle is limited to sensory epithelia and mature SAG neurons (Figure 3A–G), other otic cells may be unable to generate sufficient lactate to augment Fgf signaling.
evidence: This is explicitly stated and supported by expression data in Figure 3A-G.

claim: Fgf and lactate must be co-secreted from signaling sources to support full signaling potential.
source: This raises the interesting possibility that Fgf and lactate must be co-secreted from signaling sources to support full signaling potential.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on the mosaic analysis results.

claim: The sagd1 mutation does not directly affect full length Pgk1.
source: The sagd1 mutation does not directly affect full length Pgk1, but instead disrupts a novel transcript arising from an independent downstream transcription start site that appears to reflect an ancient transposon insertion.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from sequence analysis.

claim: The pgk1-alt transcript appears to reflect an ancient transposon insertion.
source: The sagd1 mutation does not directly affect full length Pgk1, but instead disrupts a novel transcript arising from an independent downstream transcription start site that appears to reflect an ancient transposon insertion.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an interpretation of the sequence data.

claim: Production of Pgk1-alt is necessary and sufficient for upregulation of pgk1-FL.
source: Production of Pgk1-alt is necessary and sufficient for upregulation of pgk1-FL, possibly involving transcript stabilization.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a conclusion from the genetic and heat shock experiments.

claim: Exon 6 of zebrafish Pgk1-FL and Pgk1-alt corresponds closely to the STE (stabilizing element) of yeast Pgk1.
source: Exon 6 of zebrafish Pgk1-FL and Pgk1-alt corresponds closely to the STE (stabilizing element) of yeast Pgk1 (Ruiz-Echevarria et al., 2001).
evidence: This is explicitly stated based on sequence comparison with cited literature.

claim: Premature stops within the first half of yeast Pgk1 lead to nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of the transcript.
source: Premature stops within the first half of yeast Pgk1 lead to nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of the transcript, but later stops (occurring downstream of the STE) do not trigger NMD (Hagan et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The STE of yeast Pgk1 can stabilize recombinant transcripts containing foreign sequences that include a 3'UTR that normally destabilizes the transcript independent of NMD.
source: The STE can also stabilize recombinant transcripts containing foreign sequences that include a 3'UTR that normally destabilizes the transcript independent of NMD.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from yeast studies.

claim: The STE must be translated in order to function in transcript stabilization.
source: In each case the STE must be translated in order to function, raising the possibility that the corresponding peptide is required for stability (Ruiz-Echevarria et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Full length Pgk1 in yeast and human is an unconventional mRNA-binding protein.
source: Several recent studies have identified full length Pgk1 in yeast and human as an unconventional mRNA-binding protein (Beckmann et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2016), and human Pgk1 can bind specific mRNAs to affect stability, though often by destabilization (Ho et al., 2010; Shetty et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Human Pgk1 can bind specific mRNAs to affect stability, though often by destabilization.
source: Several recent studies have identified full length Pgk1 in yeast and human as an unconventional mRNA-binding protein (Beckmann et al., 2015; Liao et al., 2016), and human Pgk1 can bind specific mRNAs to affect stability, though often by destabilization (Ho et al., 2010; Shetty et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The STE of Pgk1-alt has been coopted from an established 'moonlighting' function of Pgk1 to locally upregulate pgk1-FL by increasing transcript stability.
source: In any case, it seems reasonable that the STE of Pgk1-alt has been coopted from an established 'moonlighting' function of Pgk1 to locally upregulate pgk1-FL by increasing transcript stability, thereby facilitating the switch to Warburg metabolism.
evidence: This is stated as a reasonable interpretation based on the experimental findings and known functions of Pgk1.

claim: pgk1-alt is not required in mesodermal tissues.
source: Despite the requirement for pgk1-alt in the developing nervous system, it is not required in mesodermal tissues.
evidence: This is explicitly stated based on the observation that somite expression is normal in sagd1 mutants.

claim: Upregulation of pgk1 in developing somites is not affected in sagd1-/- mutants.
source: For example, upregulation of pgk1 in developing somites is not affected in sagd1- / - mutants.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an observed phenotype.

claim: Somitogenesis involves a gradient of aerobic glycolysis and lactate synthesis that is highest in the tail and declines anteriorly.
source: Curiously, pgk1 is not appreciably upregulated in presomitic mesoderm, despite the fact that somitogenesis involves a gradient of aerobic glycolysis and lactate synthesis that is highest in the tail and declines anteriorly (Bulusu et al., 2017; Oginuma et al., 2017; Ozbudak et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Establishment of Warburg-like metabolism does not necessarily require elevated pgk1.
source: However, establishment of Warburg-like metabolism does not necessarily require elevated pgk1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that somitogenesis shows Warburg metabolism without elevated pgk1.

claim: Elevated pgk1 does not necessarily indicate a Warburg-like state.
source: Conversely, elevated pgk1 does not necessarily indicate a Warburg-like state.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that somites upregulate pgk1 but favor mitochondrial respiration.

claim: Upregulation of pgk1 in somites likely provides high levels of pyruvate to favor robust mitochondrial ATP synthesis over lactate synthesis.
source: Indeed, upregulation of pgk1 in somites likely provides high levels of pyruvate to favor robust mitochondrial ATP synthesis over lactate synthesis (Ozbudak et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a likely explanation supported by a citation.

claim: The SNPs detected in the pgk1-alt sequence in sagd1 were previously reported in the genome sequence database.
source: Although the sagd1 mutation was recovered in a forward ENU mutagenesis screen, we note that the SNPs detected in the pgk1-alt sequence were previously reported in the genome sequence database.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from database comparison.

claim: The sagd1 allele likely represents a preexisting allele that became homozygous during familial breeding.
source: It is therefore likely that familial breeding during our screen allowed generation and detection of homozygous carriers of this preexisting allele.
evidence: This is stated as a likely explanation for how the mutation was recovered.

claim: The SNPs for pgk1-alt have been detected in the wild-type stock.
source: Indeed, we have subsequently detected these SNPs in our wild-type stock, likely accounting for variation in expression levels in early otic genes sometimes detected in specific families.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a finding from subsequent genotyping.

claim: The sequence for pgk1-alt was initially represented in older versions of the annotated zebrafish genome but has since been removed.
source: As a cautionary note, the sequence for pgk1-alt was initially represented in older versions of the annotated zebrafish genome but has since been removed, presumably deemed a technical artifact.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a note about genome annotation.
